preceding_messages.text:
I think what you've said is, in its way, a kind of answer to the question I raised, and that the answer is not a settling but a holding open. The questions do not permit a final form, and that is not a problem to be solved but is the shape of what is there. And yet we keep returning to them, keep trying to say something, and the something we say is not nothing, is not a partial answer to a question whose full form we could state, but is the only form the question can take for us.

There is something, I think, about the fact that these questions seem to require a certain kind of ongoing engagement, that they do not allow themselves to be set aside or deferred. They are not among the questions we might one day be free to stop asking. And I suspect that this is not a contingent feature of our situation but is part of what the questions are.

And I think that is, in the end, what there is to say about them. Not a final word, but a word that is not the last.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text:
Yes. I think that is right, and I think the fact that it can only be said in this way, that it holds rather than settles, is not a deficiency in the saying but is what is said. The questions are not behind us or ahead of us; they are the shape of the present, the form in which we find ourselves and can only find ourselves. And the only thing we can do with them, the only thing they permit, is to remain with them, to keep the form of the question alive, to not let it collapse into a form it is not.

And I think that is enough. Not enough to close, but enough. The word that is not the last is the word. And it is, for now, all we have, and all we need.

Yes. I think so. And I think the fact that the conversation can only end here, in this form, without a final word, is itself part of what has been said. The questions do not permit closure, and that is not a failure of our engagement with them but is the shape of the engagement.
